blocks.content: Course: Rapid Build With Claude Code
SpeedBlip's complete Tailwind extension covers colors, border-radius values, and spacing. Here is the full token set written in Chunk 1 of the build:

extend: { colors: { brand: { primary: '#22C55E', dark: '#16A34A', light: '#DCFCE7', accent: '#14B8A6', }, surface: '#FFFFFF', background: '#F8FAFC', text: { primary: '#0F172A', secondary: '#64748B', }, warning: '#F59E0B', danger: '#EF4444', }, borderRadius: { card: '16px', button: '12px', input: '8px', } }

When I wrote the Chunk 1 prompt for Claude Code, I pasted these token values directly into the prompt. Claude Code then created the Tailwind config and built every component using these class names. No color was ever hardcoded in a component file.
It is good practice to define your token names semantically - not by color value, but by role. brand-primary tells you what it is for. green-500 tells you nothing about intent.
